text:
maria: Hey team — during the AcmeCorp POC run just now we started seeing a spike of 5xxs (500/503) when concurrent clients hit ~1.2k concurrent requests. customers report intermittent failures and timeouts. Can someone triage? env: dedicated-us-west2, pool: acme-poc, model: redwood-7b-quant.

deploy-bot: [ALERT] 1789001122 - backend 503 surge on pool=acme-poc (rate=1200rps). Recent autoscale events: scale_up requested, current_replicas=2 -> pending.

sam: reading logs now, can you paste the failing request headers + sample latency?

maria: pasted sample curl and response below:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-quant","input":"summarize...","max_tokens":256}'

HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Retry-After: 3
X-Redwood-Error: server_capacity_overload
```

leo: seeing a bunch of these in infra logs:
```
inference-runtime[pid=4321] ERROR: accept loop backlog full, drop connection
kv-cache: evicting prefix cache shard=12 used=0.98
autoscaler: scale_up requested=3 reason=connection_backlog
worker[8] OOM when allocating kv cache page
```

sanjay: kv-cache thrashing + OOM on workers sounds like memory pressure during bursts. quant models can spike memory if many concurrent sequences. Are we seeing long sequence lengths?

maria: yes a few requests had ~2048 tokens in worst case, but average ~600.

sam: two-pronged approach to stabilize while we root cause: quick config changes + follow-up fixes. Suggestions:
- bump pool min_replicas to 4 temporarily
- enable burst_pool (burst capacity) for acme-poc
- add Retry-After aware client retries (exponential backoff)
- lower internal batching max latency (to avoid big batches causing memory spike)
- enable model_fallback to redwood-3b for overflow

Commands we can run now:
```bash
# increase min replicas
redwoodctl pools update acme-poc --min-replicas 4
# enable burst pool
redwoodctl pools update acme-poc --burst-pool true --burst-capacity 4
# set fallback
redwoodctl routes update acme-poc-route --fallback-model redwood-3b
```

leo: I'm applying the min_replicas bump and enabling burst_pool now. will monitor.

(leo applied changes)

deploy-bot: [INFO] 1789001220 - pool acme-poc scaled from 2 -> 4 (requested by leo). burst_pool enabled.

maria: thanks. after the change we're still seeing some 500s but much reduced, Retry-After header present and client retries succeed.

emily: logging shows autoscaler backoff delay ~45s on average before new replicas became healthy. we should reduce scale cooldown for this pool to make autoscale faster during POC bursts.

sam: good catch. change cooldown and reduce target CPU threshold for this pool to trigger earlier. Also add prefix caching for repeated prompt starts.

sanjay: digging into the worker OOMs — quant kernel allocs spike when many concurrent long sequences are served. Short-term we can enable per-request token cap and reject >1500 tokens with 429 to avoid memory storms. Long-term: we should enable progressive KV eviction and prewarm extra workers for predictable POCs.

maria: any estimate on time to fully stabilize? customer is sensitive to retries.

sam: with current mitigations (min_replicas 4 + burst_pool + retry-after clients) we should see tail errors drop in 10-15m. I'm also pushing a route-level fallback so heavy requests go to 3b automatically under pressure.

(10 minutes later)

maria: update — Service is much better, error rate from 12% -> 0.8% over last 5 min. clients report successful retries. thanks all.

leo: monitoring: 95th latency dropped from 1.8s -> 600ms, memory contention decreased. posting dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.internal/pools/acme-poc#timeseries

sam: root cause summary for postmortem: surge in concurrent long-sequence requests caused KV cache thrash and worker memory OOMs; autoscaler cooldown + health-check-probe startup delay allowed backlog to build and accept-loop dropped connections leading to 503/500. Mitigations applied: increased min_replicas, enabled burst_pool, reduced batching latency, enabled route fallback to smaller model, recommended client-side retry with Retry-After, and reduced autoscale cooldown. Follow-ups: implement faster prewarm for POC pools, adaptive token caps, and better observability on KV eviction events.

maria: we'll communicate the mitigations to the customer and ask them to implement Retry-After handling. thanks team. :pray:

sam: marking this thread resolved for now. will create a follow-up task to track infra changes and postmortem.

(closure)

deploy-bot: [RESOLVED] 1789001789 - incident mitigated on pool=acme-poc.
